newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices hold but little upside seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices hold but little upside seen.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, helped by an unchanged crude market, held relatively steady Wednesday, but bloated stocks and forecasts for mild East Coast weather still offered little hope for the bulls.
"Inventories are bulging. Unless we get some winter, I don't think prices can get any stronger," said one utility source, adding electric burns have been slow this season.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $17.50 a barrel, with unconfirmed reports of a bidder at that level, traders said.
Most forecasters expected normal to above-normal weather to dominate the East Coast into early February, and without another Arctic blast, traders said any move up would be difficult to sustain.
"(If) you don't have demand, you don't have a market," said another trader.
High sulphurs in New York also were talked unchanged, with 2.2 percent still at $16.50-75 and three percent near $16.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was still quoted in the low-$16 area, while three percent remained in the high-$14s.
No NYH or USG deals were confirmed.

Milder weather in the New York area continued to weigh on city gate gas prices, with swing off another 10-20 cents to the $3.30-3.40/mmBtu level. NYH one percent resid was still at a $2.77/mmBtu equivalent.
